findings.issue: FF-FL-7c always prints 'PASS FF-FL-7c: all password defaults are allowed dev defaults' unconditionally — even when the while-loop has already incremented ERRORS. The exit code is still correct (ERRORS is counted and the script fails at the end), but the misleading PASS line makes log output confusing when a violation occurs.
findings.suggestion: Guard the unconditional PASS print behind a check: if [[ ${ERRORS_BEFORE} -eq ${ERRORS} ]]; then echo PASS; fi (tracking ERRORS before the while loop).

findings.issue: FF-FL-8 grep fallback (used when PyYAML is absent) runs 'grep -A5 depends_on: | grep service_healthy' over the whole compose file — this matches ALL services with depends_on (keycloak and flowable both have service_healthy), not specifically the flowable block. If keycloak had service_healthy but flowable did not, the check would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Scope the grep to the flowable section: 'sed -n /^  flowable:/,/^  [a-z]/p | grep -A5 depends_on: | grep service_healthy' — or simply accept this as a minor ambiguity since yaml parsing is the primary path.

findings.issue: static-checks.sh has no static check verifying the schema isolation mechanism is configured on the SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL. FF-FL-5b only checks that the URL points to postgres:5432; it does not assert that '?currentSchema=flowable' (or SPRING_DATASOURCE_SCHEMA) is present. If the schema param were accidentally removed, only the live FF-FL-12 check (not static) would catch the regression.
findings.suggestion: Add a FF-FL-5c check: grep -qE 'SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL.*currentSchema=flowable|SPRING_DATASOURCE_SCHEMA.*flowable' to provide static-level protection for the isolation mechanism.
